tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Marijuana Records, limited jurisdiction court, A.R.S. § 36-2862

controllingAuthority.summary: The only true expungement in Arizona. Effectively mandatory: under § 36-2862(B)(3) and Rule 36(d)(3) the court must grant unless the prosecuting agency proves by clear and convincing evidence that the offense is not eligible, or the court finds the identified offense is not eligible.

eligibleDispositions: all dispositions, including acquittal and dismissal. Sentence completion is not required.
exclusions: Any marijuana offense outside the three statutory descriptions, including sale.
Any conduct occurring on or after July 12, 2021.
One petition per case number. Multiple eligible offenses under more than one case number require separate petitions.

geography.venue: Statewide Arizona law; file in the municipal or justice court that concluded the case.

destination.name: The municipal or justice court that concluded the case
destination.detail: File in person, by mail, or by e-filing where the court accepts it. The court sends the petition to the prosecuting agency within 10 days.

components.notes: Petition on the correct AOC form for a limited jurisdiction court.

components.conditionDescription: Where the petitioner has more counts than the form allows.

participantInputs.question: What is the case number, and which court concluded the case?
Which agency arrested you, and what is the incident or report number?
What was the charge, and what was the conduct — possessing, consuming or transporting marijuana, growing plants at home, or paraphernalia?
How much marijuana, or how many plants, did the case involve?
On what date did the conduct happen? Conduct on or after 12 July 2021 is not eligible.
Do you want to ask the court for a hearing?

supportingDocuments.name: Supporting exhibits: complaint, judgment and sentencing order, payment plan, lab report showing weight, DPS or FBI extract
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: The court that concluded the case, or the Arizona Department of Public Safety
supportingDocuments.conditionDescription: Optional. The form lists these as useful examples.
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Request copies from the court that concluded the case, or a criminal history extract from DPS.

manualCompletionItems.why: The petitioner signs under penalty of perjury. No notarization.

rules.filing: File in person, by mail, or by e-filing where the court accepts it. If the petition lacks enough information to identify the records, the court should refer the petitioner to the instructions and warn that it will be dismissed if the information is not filed within 45 days.
rules.fees: none. Rule 36(a)(4) bars a filing fee.
rules.feeWaiver: none. No fee waiver form is applicable because there is no filing fee.
rules.notice: The court sends the petition to the prosecuting agency within 10 days of filing. The prosecuting agency may respond within 30 days; the petitioner may reply within 15 days after a response.
rules.service: none. Rule 36(b)(2) puts transmittal to the prosecuting agency on the court.
rules.participantSignature: Petitioner signs under penalty of perjury.

selfHelpStopConditions: Prosecuting agency files a response opposing eligibility.
Court sets a hearing.
The record does not establish quantity, plant count, or paraphernalia character and the prosecutor disputes it.
Conduct date is on or after July 12, 2021.
The offense is a sale or any other non-listed marijuana offense.
The petitioner wants to challenge the underlying conviction rather than expunge it.
A denial the petitioner wants to appeal.
Immigration consequences are in play.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Seal Criminal Case Records, conviction, A.R.S. § 13-911

citations: A.R.S. § 13-911, created by SB 1294 (2021), effective January 1, 2023, amended by SB 1639 (2024)
Ariz. R. Crim. P. 36.1, as amended by order R-24-0049, permanent amendments effective January 1, 2025
controllingAuthority.summary: Sealing, not expungement. Section 13-911(D) says the court shall grant if granting is in the best interests of the petitioner and the public's safety. Treat as discretionary for product copy.

eligibleDispositions: convicted, all sentence terms complete including all monetary obligations and victim restitution
exclusions: § 13-911(O): dangerous offense as defined in § 13-105; dangerous crime against children as defined in § 13-705; serious offense or violent or aggravated felony as defined in § 13-706; any offense with an element of discharge, use, or threatening exhibition of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument, or knowing infliction of serious physical injury on another person; sex trafficking under § 13-1307; any class 2, 3, 4, or 5 felony under Title 13, chapter 14 or chapter 35.1.
Rule 36.1(b) makes a person ineligible to file if a petition was denied in the past three years. Section 13-911(L) separately bars a new petition until three years after the denial.

§ 13-911(N) and Rule 36.1(f)(2): if the petitioner has a charge pending or is charged after filing, and that charge could result in an unsealable conviction or extend the waiting period, the court may not rule until it disposes of that charge.

waitingPeriods.duration: 10 years from completion of the nonmonetary terms of probation or sentence and discharge by the court

waitingPeriods.condition: Stacking rule, § 13-911(F): a person who sealed records and then commits a felony
waitingPeriods.duration: That felony's class period plus five more years

geography.venue: Statewide Arizona law; file in the court of conviction.

destination.name: The court of conviction
destination.detail: One petition per case. Each court where the person was convicted needs its own petition. If the person appealed from a limited jurisdiction court, a separate superior court petition is needed to reach those records.

components.conditionDescription: The form is court-facing and contains the judge's findings. Some courts expect the petitioner to lodge it. Verify per court.

participantInputs.question: What is the case number, and which court convicted you?
What was the offence, its statute section, and its class?
On what date did you complete the nonmonetary terms of probation or sentence and get discharged by the court?
Have all fines, fees and victim restitution been paid?
Have you had records sealed in Arizona before?
Has a sealing petition of yours been denied in the last three years?
Do you have any charge pending now?
In your own words, why is sealing in your best interests and consistent with public safety?

supportingDocuments.name: Certificate of absolute discharge from ADOC
supportingDocuments.conditionDescription: Strongly encouraged by the form where applicable.
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Request the certificate of absolute discharge from ADOC.

supportingDocuments.name: Order of discharge from probation
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: The court that placed you on probation
supportingDocuments.conditionDescription: Strongly encouraged by the form where applicable.
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that placed you on probation for the order of discharge.

manualCompletionItems.why: Signature under penalty of perjury. No notarization.

manualCompletionItems.item: Notice of new charges after filing
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Ongoing duty stated on the form
manualCompletionItems.why: The form imposes a continuing duty to notify the court of new charges after filing.

rules.filing: File in the court identified by § 13-911(C) for the situation — here, the court of conviction.
rules.fees: No statutory filing fee identified, and multiple municipal courts publish that they charge none for this petition. Confirm per court. Unresolved statewide. Under § 13-911(H) the DPS director may charge an investigation fee, and under § 13-911(I)(3) DPS may charge a successful petitioner a record-correction fee.
rules.feeWaiver: DPS fees are waived for an indigent petitioner and for a petitioner found not guilty or whose case was dismissed or not prosecuted where the petition is filed under § 13-911(C)(2) or (C)(3).
rules.notice: The court notifies DPS and requests a report of the petitioner's state and federal arrests, prosecutions, and convictions. The clerk provides a copy of the petition to the prosecutor. If the victim requested post-conviction notice, the prosecutor notifies the victim, who has a right to be present and heard. The court may not grant or deny for at least 60 days unless it has notice that the prosecutor and all noticed victims do not object.
rules.service: none by the petitioner. The court provides the copy to the prosecuting agency.

selfHelpStopConditions: Prosecutor files an objection or requests a hearing.
A victim exercises the right to be heard.
Offense class or the § 13-911(O) screen is genuinely ambiguous.
Restitution or court debt is unpaid or disputed.
A prior denial inside three years.
A stacking question under § 13-911(F).
Pending charges.
The person needs relief that reaches a fingerprint clearance card determination.
A limited jurisdiction appeal that requires a second superior court petition the participant does not want to handle.
Immigration consequences.
Any request to attack the conviction itself.

citations: Ariz. R. Crim. P. 41, Forms 31(a) and 31(b), as amended by order R-24-0049, effective January 1, 2025
controllingAuthority.summary: Set aside the judgment of guilt. It is not sealing and not expungement. Discretionary: § 13-905(C) lists seven factors the court must consider. The record stays public with a set-aside annotation.

eligibleDispositions: conviction, after fulfilment of the conditions of probation or sentence and discharge by the court
exclusions: § 13-905(P): a dangerous offense; an offense requiring registration under § 13-3821; an offense with a finding of sexual motivation under § 13-118; a felony offense in which the victim is a minor under fifteen.

destination.detail: One application per case number, and each count is addressed individually. The state or the victim must file any objection within 30 days after the application is filed.

components.notes: Required as a lodged proposed order in practice. The order includes a finding that the prosecutor received a copy of the application.

controllingAuthority.summary: If the court did not include a certificate in the set-aside order, the person may later apply for one after meeting the § 13-905(K) requirements. It is expressly not a recommendation or sponsorship.
